videos.title: New Minecraft Bedrock Addon Lets Solves Inventory Management!
videos.description:
Minecraft has almost a thousand blocks… and you get 36 slots and NINE hotbar items. 😤

Bedrock Hotbar Shuffle fixes that. One keybind. Your entire inventory. No menus, no swapping, no dragging items around like a lunatic.

If you build on Bedrock, this is the addon you've been quietly rage-quitting about for years.

⚡ WHAT IT DOES
Bedrock Hotbar Shuffle adds a keybindable macro that shifts your active hotbar through all 3 extra rows of your inventory — instantly. Tools stay put. Food stays put. Your gradient blocks stay exactly where you sorted them. You just… shuffle to them.

No more one-at-a-time block swaps. No more moving your pickaxe out of the way to grab a slab. No more inventory that looks like a carnival after it left town. 🎪

🛠️ SETUP (takes ~30 seconds)

Install the addon to your world from CurseForge
Open Settings → Keyboard & Mouse → scroll to Macros
Add /shuffle:down and /shuffle:up to any two slots
Bind them to an ALT + key combo (ALT + Q / ALT + E works great — or any key or mouse button you like)

That's it. Your whole inventory, one button away.

📥 DOWNLOAD — 100% FREE
CurseForge: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft-bedrock/addons/hotbar-shuffle

Mobs in bedrock only count as "tamed" if they are in fenced in, bred, are nametagged, or have specific player interactions. To get around this, you need to breed new sheep, nametag, or manually shear them to get them tagged as "tamed"

In this Minecraft Bedrock 1.20+ tutorial, Alaydriem shows how to build an incredibly simple and safe, fully AFK-able Raid Farm! This Raid Farm is incredibly easy to build, reliable, and safe from ravagers, vex, evoker claws; and will generate an infinite supply of totems, enchanted books, emeralds, and other useful gear, weapons, and supplies!

IMPORTANT NOTES:
1. This farm is designed for a ticking radius of 4 (the normal for Bedrock), a larger ticking radius might prevent the pillagers from spawning in the lower raid cell.
2. Your AFK spot needs to be directly above the spawn spot on the lower cell. Additionally, I recommend having an auto-hotkey, or a rubber band around your controller to move you back and around a bit, as the movement will help with ensuring pillagers in the lower cell spawn. This isn't strictly necessary, but it helps with the lower spawn cells.
3. If the tridents get bumped, rethrow them. This only happens if you have high latency to your instance or are in a laggy world/area.
4. Before leaving the farm, make sure you clear any stacked bad omen on you. Use the XP you gathered to repair any tools/armor/make enchantments, and the best way to ensure you have the bad omen cleared is to jump off the top and respawn at a nearby bed. Bad omen stacks but you can't see and always clear the stacks, so forcing a respawn is the best way to ensure you don't trigger a raid at another villager.
